claims.text: FeNiCrCoCu coatings can maintain wear resistance at elevated temperatures.
The primary cause of high-temperature wear resistance is the in-situ formation of a stable, adherent oxide-based tribofilm.
An intact oxide tribofilm reduces abrasive and adhesive wear.
Disruption or absence of the oxide tribofilm causes accelerated wear.
The coating is several micrometers thick and deposited or sprayed onto a conventional steel substrate.
Applying a high-entropy alloy as a coating on a lower-cost conventional substrate is an economically viable alternative to making the alloy in bulk.
Increasing the test temperature from room temperature to about 600 °C will alter the wear response relative to the room-temperature baseline.
Elevated temperature promotes formation of an oxide layer on the coating's contact surface.
The oxide layer decreases direct asperity contact between the coating and counterface.
The thermal stability and mechanical integrity of the oxide layer govern wear performance over the tested temperature range.
Grain-scale microstructural stability within FeNiCrCoCu also mediates its wear response.
When the oxide tribofilm remains intact, friction coefficient and wear rate will remain stable or decrease at intermediate and high temperatures relative to room temperature.
When the oxide layer is disrupted or cannot form consistently, wear rate will increase markedly.
The proposed mechanism is applicable from room temperature to approximately 600 °C under moderate coating loads.
Above approximately 600 °C or under more severe loading, oxide stability and coating microstructure may change enough that the proposed mechanism no longer holds.
Oxygen content, coating-substrate interactions, and oxide composition may affect high-temperature tribofilm formation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts that absent or disrupted oxide accompanied by increased wear supports the proposed mechanism, but the falsification rule says that increasing wear together with failure to observe a stable oxide tribofilm would disprove it. That result is confirmatory rather than falsifying under the stated causal model.
